title: Generation Failure Mode Triage data
note: Six failure modes from the Chapter 5 table and eight defective-MicroSim cases drawn from them. Console messages are simulated but written in the form Chrome prints them.

modes.name: Hallucinated API
modes.definition: A call to a function, method or option that does not exist in the library, written by the model because it looks plausible.
modes.symptom: Console error about an unknown function
modes.cause: The model wrote a call that the library does not have.
modes.repair: Check the name in the library's reference and replace it with the documented call.
modes.tell: a console error naming a function or method that no release of the library has

modes.name: Library version drift
modes.definition: The growing mismatch between the library release the code was written for and the release it runs on, which turns once-correct calls into errors or changed behavior.
modes.symptom: Code that once worked now errors or draws differently
modes.cause: Code and library versions no longer match.
modes.repair: Compare the pin in main.html with the code's assumptions, then migrate the call or restore the pin.
modes.tell: code that used to work, a pin or editor release that changed, and a call that is real in another release

modes.name: Control in drawing area
modes.definition: A slider or button placed inside the drawing region instead of the control region below drawHeight.
modes.symptom: A slider or button floats over the drawing
modes.repair: Position the control relative to drawHeight, for example drawHeight + 5.
modes.tell: a control sitting on the aliceblue drawing region while the console stays clean

modes.name: Non-responsive canvas
modes.definition: A canvas that keeps one width when the window or its container is resized.
modes.symptom: Canvas stays one width when the window resizes
modes.cause: A hard-coded width and no updateCanvasSize().
modes.repair: Restore the standard resize pattern: updateCanvasSize() in setup() and windowResized() with resizeCanvas().
modes.tell: a defect that changes with window width: an empty strip or a cut-off on the right side

modes.name: Wrong iframe height
modes.definition: An iframe whose height is not the canvas height plus 2, so the chapter shows too little or too much of the MicroSim.
modes.symptom: Controls are clipped in the chapter
modes.cause: The iframe height differs from the canvas height plus 2.
modes.repair: Run the height sync utility (sync-iframe-heights.py) so every iframe uses CANVAS_HEIGHT + 2.
modes.tell: a sim that is fine fullscreen but cut off at the bottom inside the chapter page

modes.name: Text with an outline
modes.definition: Text drawn while a stroke color is still active, so every glyph gets an outline and looks heavy or fuzzy.
modes.cause: A stroke was still active when text() was drawn.
modes.repair: Call noStroke() before every text() call.
modes.tell: lettering that looks wrong while shapes, controls and the console are all fine

cases.title: Slider never appears
cases.symptom: The canvas shows as an empty white rectangle. No title, no ball and no speed slider appear, at any window width.

console.text: Uncaught TypeError: createRangeSlider is not a function

cases.evidence: the console names createRangeSlider, which the p5.js reference does not list in any release. The documented call is createSlider(min, max, value, step).

confusions.version-drift: Drift needs a call that was real in some release. createRangeSlider never existed, and nothing about the pin changed.

cases.title: Slider floats over the ball
cases.symptom: On a laptop the speed slider sits inside the ball's box, right where the ball bounces. The control region below it is empty.
cases.evidence: the slider is drawn inside the aliceblue drawing region at a fixed height and the console is clean. The code positions it at a hard-coded y instead of drawHeight + 5.

confusions.iframe-height: A wrong iframe height clips controls at the bottom of the page; it never moves a control up into the drawing.

cases.title: Board photo vanished after a pin bump
cases.symptom: Last term this breadboard sim showed a photo of the board. The only change since then: main.html now loads p5.js 2.3.2. The drawing region is empty.

console.text: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')

cases.evidence: the code worked before and only the pin changed. The sketch loads its image in preload(), which p5.js 2.x removed, so the image variable is never set.

confusions.hallucinated-api: A hallucinated API names a function that never existed. Here the failing code is real 1.x code, and the error only began when the pin moved to 2.x.

cases.title: Fuzzy, heavy labels
cases.symptom: The title and the Speed label look blurry and bold, as if outlined, although the font size is right. Shapes and controls look normal at every width.
cases.evidence: only the lettering is wrong. A stroke() call made for the box border is still active when text() runs, so every glyph is outlined.

cases.title: Bottom row cut off in the chapter
cases.symptom: Opened fullscreen, the sim is fine. Embedded in the chapter page, the bottom row of controls is cut in half.
cases.evidence: fullscreen shows everything, so the sketch's own layout is correct. Only the container is too short: the iframe height is less than the canvas height plus 2.

confusions.non-responsive: A non-responsive canvas fails on the right side as the width changes. This defect is at the bottom and appears only inside the chapter.

cases.title: Reset button does nothing
cases.symptom: The ball bounces and the slider works. A Reset button appears, but clicking it never moves the ball back to the start.

console.text: Uncaught TypeError: position.reset is not a function

cases.evidence: the error appears only when the line runs, on the click, and names a method p5.Vector does not have. The documented method is set().

confusions.control-in-drawing: The button is in the right place and responds to the click; the error happens inside the function it calls.

cases.title: Empty strip on the right
cases.symptom: In a wide browser window the canvas stops at 400 pixels and leaves an empty strip on the right. On a phone the right side is cut off.
cases.evidence: the defect depends on the window width and appears on the right side. The sketch creates a fixed 400-pixel canvas and never calls updateCanvasSize().

confusions.iframe-height: The iframe height controls the bottom edge. A gap or cut-off on the right comes from the canvas width.

cases.title: Curved arrows turned into spikes
cases.symptom: After the site moved to p5.js 2.x, the curved arrows in a workflow diagram draw as jagged straight segments. Nothing else changed.
cases.evidence: the code once drew correctly and there is no error at all. bezierVertex() still exists in 2.x but takes one control point per call, so the old six-number calls draw differently.

confusions.hallucinated-api: A hallucinated call fails with an error because the function does not exist. A clean console plus changed drawing after an upgrade points to drift.
